newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Sinaloa state to plant soybeans - report.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Sinaloa state to plant soybeans - report.

text.p: Mexico's northwestern state of Sinaloa will plant 5,000 hectares of soybeans this spring, national news agency Notimex reported Monday.

Manuel Beltran Lopez, spokesman for the Fund for the Investigation, Development of Plant Health for the Valle del Fuerte in Sinaloa, told Notimex the plantings were expected to yield 10,000 tonnes of soybeans.
Beltran said specific farm zones had been pinpointed for the plantings to avoid incidences of white fly which has plagued the crop in the state in the past.
Sinaloa had stopped planting soybeans for at least the last two crop cycles because of white fly infestation and because of price restraints.
Mexico's only state to have consistently planted soybean in recent years has been Tamaulipas.
